edits.content:
version: 2

sources:
  - name: raw
    schema: raw
    description: >
      Public signals landed by `gta6 ingest` as Parquet under data/raw/ and loaded by
      `gta6 load`. Every table is rebuilt from the files on each load; the newest pull
      wins per key. No post text, handles or usernames are stored.
    tables:
      - name: wiki_pageviews
        description: Daily English Wikipedia pageviews by users (all access) per article.
      - name: trends_interest
        description: >
          Google Trends relative interest (0-100) per term and day. Values only compare
          within one request_id; Google rescales every request to its own peak.
      - name: bluesky_daily_hits
        description: >
          Bluesky public search hitsTotal for one quoted seed phrase (optionally plus "gta")
          bounded to one UTC day. hits_total is NULL when the call failed.
      - name: hn_daily_hits
        description: >
          Hacker News (Algolia) nbHits for one quoted seed phrase (optionally plus "gta")
          over stories and comments in one UTC day. NULL when the call failed.
      - name: reddit_items
        description: >
          Reddit posts and comments (Arctic Shift archive) that matched a day-off seed in a
          tracked subreddit, with flags computed from the text at ingest. Text is discarded.
      - name: reddit_coverage
        description: >
          One row per (subreddit, kind, seed, weekly slice) we asked Arctic Shift for, with
          whether paging completed, was capped, or failed.

with source as (
    select * from {{ source('raw', 'wiki_pageviews') }}
)

select
    article,
    cast(timezone('UTC', ts) as date) as view_date,
    cast(views as bigint) as views
from source
where granularity = 'daily'

-- Each Trends request is scaled to its own 0-100, so we keep exactly one request per
-- (term group, geo, study year): the newest. Mixing requests would mix scales.
with source as (
    select
        *,
        cast(split_part(request_id, '-', 3) as integer) as study_year
    from {{ source('raw', 'trends_interest') }}
),

newest as (
    select term_group, geo, study_year, max(request_id) as request_id
    from source
    group by term_group, geo, study_year
)

select
    source.request_id,
    source.study_year,
    source.term_group,
    source.geo,
    source.term,
    source.day as interest_date,
    cast(source.interest as integer) as interest,
    source.is_partial
from source
inner join newest
    on source.request_id = newest.request_id

select
    day as hit_date,
    seed,
    gta_filter,
    query,
    cast(hits_total as bigint) as hits_total,
    hits_total is not null as is_available,
    observed_at
from {{ source('raw', 'bluesky_daily_hits') }}

select
    day as hit_date,
    seed,
    gta_filter,
    query,
    cast(hits_total as bigint) as hits_total,
    hits_total is not null as is_available,
    observed_at
from {{ source('raw', 'hn_daily_hits') }}

declarations.description: One row per Wikipedia article per UTC day: daily user pageviews.

population.rule: Daily-granularity rows only; the per-article API serves no hourly data.

view_date.description: UTC day. The raw ts is a UTC midnight stored as TIMESTAMPTZ; converted explicitly so the session time zone cannot shift it.

views.description: Pageviews by users (agent=user), all access methods.

assumptions.decision: Which day a timestamp belongs to
assumptions.detail: explore showed ts rendered at +01:00/+02:00 in a local session; the API's timestamps are UTC midnights

declarations.description: One row per Trends term per day, from the newest request for each (term group, geo, study year).

population.rule: Only the newest request per (term_group, geo, study_year); older pulls are dropped because each request has its own 0-100 scale.

request_id.description: The Trends request the value came from; values only compare within one request.

term_group.description: 'day_off' (call in sick, sick day, PTO, day off work) or 'hype' (GTA 6). Requested separately.

interest_date.description: The day Google reports, in Google's own day boundaries.

interest.description: Relative search interest; 100 is the peak of that request.

is_partial.description: Google marks the latest day partial while it is still filling in.

assumptions.decision: How to combine repeated Trends pulls
assumptions.chosen: keep only the newest request per (term_group, geo, study_year)
assumptions.detail: Trends rescales each request; averaging requests would mix scales
request_id is written as <group>-<geo>-<year>-<stamp> by gta6_impact.ingest.trends

declarations.description: One row per Bluesky search (seed phrase x gta filter) per UTC day: the hitsTotal Bluesky reported.

population.rule: Every query we asked, including failed ones (hits_total NULL).

gta_filter.description: 'any' = the phrase alone; 'gta' = the phrase plus the word gta.

hits_total.null_rule: NULL when the Bluesky call failed: unavailable, never zero.
hits_total.description: Matches Bluesky reports for the query in that UTC day.

observed_at.description: When the count was read (counts can move as indexes update).

assumptions.chosen: (hit_date, seed, gta_filter): one search per key per day
assumptions.detail: probe .dex/review/06-*.json: distinct (day, seed, gta_filter) equals row count. observed_at is unique only because every request is timed separately; it is not the grain

assumptions.chosen: every query this source was asked, independent of the other search source
assumptions.detail: Bluesky and Hacker News are searched with the same seeds on the same days, but neither is a parent of the other

assumptions.chosen: kept with hits_total NULL and is_available false

declarations.description: One row per Hacker News search (seed phrase x gta filter) per UTC day: Algolia's nbHits over stories and comments.

population.rule: Every query we asked, including failed ones (hits_total NULL).

gta_filter.description: 'any' = the phrase alone; 'gta' = the phrase plus the word gta.

hits_total.null_rule: NULL when the Hacker News call failed: unavailable, never zero.
hits_total.description: Matches Hacker News reports for the query in that UTC day.

observed_at.description: When the count was read (counts can move as indexes update).

assumptions.chosen: (hit_date, seed, gta_filter): one search per key per day
assumptions.detail: probe .dex/review/05-*.json: distinct (day, seed, gta_filter) equals row count. observed_at is unique only because every request is timed separately; it is not the grain

assumptions.chosen: every query this source was asked, independent of the other search source
assumptions.detail: Bluesky and Hacker News are searched with the same seeds on the same days, but neither is a parent of the other

assumptions.chosen: kept with hits_total NULL and is_available false
